headline: India Orders Bitchat Code Disabled
deck: A three-hour notice to GitHub named general-purpose communications repositories and objected to their architecture. The code remained public after the deadline.
body: India’s cybercrime coordination centre directed GitHub to disable three Bitchat repository URLs within three hours. The notice, dated 23 July and published by project co-creator Jack Dorsey, invoked Section 79(3)(b) of the Information Technology Act and Rule 3(1)(d) of the 2021 intermediary rules. [E1] It threatened the platform’s safe-harbour protection and further liability if GitHub did not act. [E1] The order supplied a deadline before it supplied a public docket.

Its operative complaint addressed the software’s design. The notice said Bitchat permits anonymous communication without mandatory registration, phone verification or central logging, and can impede lawful interception during internet shutdowns. [E1] It did not identify a message, file or named criminal act inside the repositories. The alleged unlawful information was a capacity to communicate.

Bitchat’s own documentation describes Bluetooth low-energy mesh networking, store-and-forward relays and online channels using Nostr. [E2] Users do not need accounts, phone numbers or a central server. [E2] Devices already carrying the software can exchange messages across nearby relays when ordinary internet access is absent. Removing a repository would constrain distribution and audit, while leaving installed copies able to speak.

The named repositories remained publicly reachable on 25 July. [E2] GitHub’s government-takedown archive had no corresponding India entry at the reporting cutoff. [E3] Public access does not establish that GitHub rejected the demand, and a view from outside India cannot exclude every regional restriction. It establishes the narrower enforcement result: the requested global disappearance had not occurred.

India’s intermediary rules can require a host to remove unlawful information after a qualifying government notice. The order stretches that mechanism across source code that hosts no particular conversation. Civil-liberties advocates called the move unconstitutional and demanded that authorities publish such notices. [E4] Their stronger argument rests on the missing object: a removal duty needs something more specific than disfavoured architecture.

Public order supplies the serious null. Anonymous mesh tools can help people coordinate violence, evade lawful surveillance or operate during restrictions imposed for safety. The government could strengthen that case by naming a cognisable offence, publishing the evidentiary link and defending a tailored order in court. None of those discriminators appeared in the public artifact. [E1][E3][E4]

The three-hour clock has therefore exposed the notice’s enforcement gap. A state can pressure one distribution point, but public source code has forks, local copies and independent build paths. GitHub may still geoblock, remove or litigate. On the first deadline, the government ordered a protocol to forget how it works, and the repository kept remembering.
